To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the p53 mutation is a prognostic and predictive factor in breast cancer, that the p53 gene status may be used to stratify patients with high risk BC into two groups with different prognosis and sensitivity to medical treatment, that the p 53 gene analysis is useful to identify the patients who may be candidates for a more aggressive adjuvant therapy, and that the p  53 mutation may be used as a marker of response to chemotherapy in advanced breast cancer.

p53 mutations are associated to a worse prognosis in breast cancer and to resistance to chemotherapy; the FAMA method allows the identification of p53 mutations in a high proportion of breast carcinomas, and the evaluation of the p-53 status may be useful for predicting prognosis and sensitivity to medical treatments.

the evaluation of p53 status in breast cancer and the identification of molecular markers of response to therapy, in order to improve the treatment of breast cancer patients.
the development and validation of molecular diagnostic strategies in order to improve the prognostic and predictive value of the clinical evaluation in breast cancer patients.
the development of a molecular diagnostic tool to improve the therapeutic approach of breast cancer, in particular of high risk patients.

the analysis of the p 53 gene performed by means of FAMA in high-risk breast patients with > or < 10 involved axillar nodes may help identify two subsets of patients with poorer prognosis and two subsets with better prognosis, respectively, potentially responsive to different medical treatments.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

p53 analysis in breast cancer patients is a useful tool to identify a subset of patients who may be candidates for adjuvant chemotherapy, and to identify a subset who may benefit from a less aggressive approach.
the p53 gene analysis is a useful tool for the management of breast cancer patients, especially for those at high risk of relapse.
the p53 status is a powerful prognostic factor, which can be easily and reliably determined by FAMA, a simple, fast and cost-effective technique.

p53 status can be used as a predictive marker of prognosis and sensitivity to medical treatments.
